PROJECT NO. 58481
COMMENTS of Occidental Permian, LTD.
INTRODUCTION
Occidental Permian, Ltd. (“OPL”) appreciates the opportunity to submit comments on the Discussion Draft §25.194 posted by Staff of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission Staff”) which would set the standards and criteria for an electric utility, including a municipally owned utility and electric cooperative, to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network.  The Commission Staff invited comments by December 19, 2025. As such these comments are timely filed.
OPL owns and operates industrial facilities located in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (“ERCOT”) footprint.  Timely access to reliable and affordable electricity is paramount to our operations and as such OPL has a vested interest in the interconnection standards for large load customers.  
COMMENTS BY SECTION
(l)	ERCOT operational standards. 
ERCOT may establish operational standards for large load customers to ensure system reliability.
A large load customer must comply with operational standards, developed through ERCOT protocols, as a condition for interconnection and continued operation of the customer's load.
OPL believes this section is not appropriate as Senate Bill (SB) 6 did not authorize ERCOT to establish or enforce new operational standards on interconnecting large loads and OPL questions the authority for ERCOT to do so. OPL recommends the Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission”) remove this proposed subsection and allow stakeholders to focus their efforts on the sections of the rule required by SB 6.  
Additionally, OPL believes there is a clear distinction between Market Participants (“MP”) and retail customers.  OPL operates both pure retail customer sites and sites which are registered as ERCOT MPs in order to participate in a portion of the wholesale market, specifically providing Responsive Reserve Service (“RRS”).  For those sites providing RRS, we have actively chosen to have a relationship with ERCOT by registering as a MP and we are responsible for complying with the applicable protocols for RRS participation.  In return, we have an opportunity to offer our products and be compensated for any services we provide.  Conversely, for those loads which are purely retail, we are not an ERCOT MP and are not eligible to receive compensation for wholesale activity.  For our pure retail loads we fully depend on our utility and retail electric provider for any service issues and to act on our behalf in the wholesale markets. Further, all retail loads support payment for grid reliability services and the buildout of transmission facilities; not all MPs are required to fund these services.  OPL believes that establishing requirements for pure retail large load customers would be inappropriate, given the structural distinctions between retail customers and Market Participants.
Equally concerning for OPL is the generic “one-size-fits-all” approach we have seen in past attempts from EROCT to impose operational requirements on retail customers.  Large loads span a number of industries with different operational characteristics. Even within a specific site, the operational characteristics can vary depending on what processes or equipment are running at any given time.  We’ve seen this approach result in unreasonable requirement proposals.  Requiring industrials to tolerate conditions on the electric grid that their equipment is not designed to manage will likely lead to reliability and economic consequences, such as damaged equipment which can result in operational downtime. Taking it a step further and requiring compliance with operational standards imposed by ERCOT as a condition of continued operation imposes additional risk to retail customers and may compromise key industries that contribute to the state’s economy. These additional risks would be unique to ERCOT as they are not required in other jurisdictions. 

CONCLUSION
OPL appreciates this opportunity to comment and looks forward to continued discussions. 

Respectfully submitted,

Occidental Permian, Ltd. 

			

Melissa Trevino
5 Greenway Plaza, Suite 110
Melissa_Trevino@oxy.com
281-323-8801
